Hi Samir / Elena —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and the open items we discussed around performance / streaming SLOs so we can align next steps: 

Summary of FinTechCo targets (per call)
- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target: <= 300 ms (goal: 200–250 ms for top priority flows)
- Streaming: one-way server->client streaming for incremental updates (customer preference: SSE, but WebSocket was mentioned as fallback)
- Chunk cadence: target ~150–250 ms between chunks during steady streaming; low-latency bursts ok for first 1–2 chunks
- Throughput & concurrency: sustained 50 req/s with 2,000 concurrent connected clients; burst to 200 req/s for short windows
- Model note: medium-sized LLaMA2-style variant (est. 8–12B) with typical response lengths 50–200 tokens

Open questions / asks from Redwood (we'll need these for accurate sizing and a short POC):
1) Preferred streaming transport: SSE, WebSocket, or both for the POC?
2) Target client network characteristics (median egress latency, any proxies or TLS termination in front of clients)
3) Are we measuring TTFT at the client (first rendered byte) or server-side accept? We typically instrument both but need to match measurement definitions.
4) Do you have existing sample logs or a short trace we can use to reproduce chunk cadence and payload sizes?

Attachments: SLO-metrics-proposal.xlsx (initial sizing + perf test plan).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm preferred transport and share sample traces (Samir) — by EOD Wed
- Redwood to propose a 2-week POC plan and a perf target baseline (we'll include a synthetic harness that emulates 2,000 concurrent SSE clients) — by Thu
- Quick sync to lock the POC window (30 min) — can you do Thu or Fri?

Thanks — looping Hannah to help with infra/POC details.

Thanks Samir — good datapoints. Looping in Marissa (solutions) + Hannah (infra) to scope the POC and proposed perf targets. Quick answers up front: 

- Transport: Redwood supports SSE and WebSocket. For one-way streaming SSE is simpler and performs very well in our hosted and Dedicated environments; WebSocket works for bi-directional or mobile SDK scenarios.
- TTFT measurement: we will instrument both client-side (first byte) and server-side (request accepted -> first token emitted). We'll align on a single definition for SLA reporting during the POC.
- Chunk cadence & payload: we typically recommend flushing small chunks frequently — target 100–200 ms cadence for steady-state. For the first chunk we flush as soon as the model emits the first tokens to minimize TTFT. Typical chunk size: ~10–30 tokens (or ~512 bytes) to keep per-chunk overhead low.
- Concurrency & connections: for SSE we recommend horizontal scaling of proxies and keeping keepalive ~60s; Redwood Dedicated can handle 2k concurrent SSE connections per pool depending on node size — we'll size the pool in the SLO-metrics spreadsheet.

I've attached a sample Redwood TTFT log (redwood-ttft-sample.log) and a simple network diagram (network-diagram.png) showing where the edge proxy sits. We'll update the SLO spreadsheet with two rows: Hosted baseline (expected TTFT ~300–400 ms for 8–12B depending on tokenization and model latency) and Dedicated baseline (expected TTFT ~200–300 ms). Exact numbers require a short perf run.

Proposed POC plan (high level):
- Step 0: confirm transport (you said SSE ok) + synthetic dataset (you'll provide by Wed)
- Step 1: Redwood deploys a test endpoint and perf harness emulating 500/1,000/2,000 concurrent SSE clients (1 day)
- Step 2: Run baseline perf with target model & payload sizes; collect client+server TTFT metrics (2 days)
- Step 3: Tune batching/kv-caching/quantization profile + re-run to hit TTFT goal (3–4 days)
- Deliverable: perf report + recommended config and estimated cost per 1M tokens.

Can we schedule the 30-min POC kickoff Thu 19:00–20:00 UTC / Thu 13:00–14:00 PT?

Best,

Hi Samir / Elena —

Quick technical follow-up from my side on the feasibility and proposed test parameters so we have a clean measurement plan. We're happy to run the POC using SSE as the primary transport and WebSocket for a quick validation of mobile behavior.

Measurement definitions (to avoid surprises):
- Client-side TTFT: time from client request send to first byte rendered in client UI (we'll provide a small client instrument that emits this metric)
- Server-side TTFT: time from request accept in Redwood front-end to first token emitted by model runtime

Initial targets (for the POC):
- Goal TTFT (client-side): <= 250 ms for priority flows on Dedicated; <= 300 ms on Hosted for 8–12B model with adjusted batching/kv-cache.
- Chunk cadence: flush chunks at ~120 ms cadence in steady-state; first chunk flush < 80 ms where model emits early tokens. This cadence balances socket overhead vs. perceived latency.
- Chunk size: target ~10–25 tokens (~256–512 bytes) per chunk in tests; we'll capture empirical size distribution from your sample logs.
- Throughput & concurrency test matrix: baseline runs at 50 req/s sustained with 500, 1,000, and 2,000 concurrent SSE clients. Burst tests at 200 req/s for 60s windows.

Network & infra asks from our side (we'll need these before the perf window):
1) Confirm edge proxy keepalive and any idle timeout values (we recommend keepalive >= 60s and idle timeout > 120s for long-lived SSE).
2) Confirm whether TLS is terminated at your edge or we should terminate at Redwood (affects RTT).
3) If possible, provide a 1-minute pcap or synthetic trace and a small sample payload (we can scrub PII).

POC timeline (2 weeks recommended):
- Week 1: deploy + baseline runs + data collection
- Week 2: tuning (batching, quantization) + final runs + report

Action items:
- Samir: confirm SSE for POC + share sample trace and preferred kickoff slot (EOD Wed)
- Aditya: schedule kickoff and provision test endpoint once artifacts are in
- Hannah/Marissa: we'll prepare an infra sizing note and a recommended Redwood config for the POC

Happy to jump on a quick 15–20 min call if you want to go line-by-line on the measurement plan.

Cheers,
